newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Papua mercenaries say contract terminated.
newsitem.headline: Papua mercenaries say contract terminated.

text.p: Papua New Guinea has cancelled its contract with British-based Sandline International for the hire of mercenaries to help its battle with rebels on Bougainville island, a departing helicopter pilot said on Wednesday.
"The contract's terminated. It's as simple as that. It's better for both sides," the pilot told reporters in Singapore.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan told a news conference in Port Moresby earlier in the day he was considering cancelling the controversial contract, "but we must not be too premature about making that decision".
The pilots, who declined to be identified, said they had arrived in Papua New Guinea on Sunday and were told on Monday to leave. They spoke in transit in Singapore on their way home to South Africa.
"The contract was stopped by mutual agreement," said one, who added the other 34 mercenaries sent to the country would leave once logistical problems, which he did not specify, were sorted out.
